theResultThatMatters.claim: The gate is reachable and the curation works. MEASURED on the LIVE ROUTER, not the simulator.
theResultThatMatters.tool: get_agent_coin_qualification - runs the full five-gate ladder with no LLM call and no capital
theResultThatMatters.summary: 7 of 8 qualify. Both long and short candidateLevels resolve ok on every passing coin. requiredCount and requiredConditions both NOT_ENFORCED. The one rejection is ETH at 61 against the 65 floor - a 4-point miss, which is the gate discriminating rather than blocking.
theResultThatMatters.whyThisIsTheHeadline: The whole design rested on an UNMEASURED assumption: that the live router computes its aggregate the way simulate_aggregate_score does - a weighted mean over TRIGGERED signals only, with allocation-0 signals leaving the denominator. If the router had instead averaged over all 84 materialised signals, 0.65 would have been unreachable and this would have joined the 12 coins already reading AGGREGATE_BELOW_MIN. The router agrees. The assumption is now measured.

howTheGateWasSet.method: Derived from an empty interval, not picked. simulate_aggregate_score on this exact card: ETH 0.5648 REJECT, ballast-only floor 0.6083 REJECT, BTC 0.7699 ADMIT, SOL 0.7831 ADMIT, HYPE 0.8560 ADMIT. Highest reject to lowest admit is a 16.2-point gap with nothing in it; 0.65 sits inside.
howTheGateWasSet.curationIsTheEdge: The aggregate is a weighted mean over TRIGGERED signals only, so every frequently-triggering LOW scorer that carries weight is a direct subtraction. Excluding them lifted BTC from 48 unweighted to 77 and SOL from 54 to 78 at the same instant - same tape, same moment, purely from curation.
howTheGateWasSet.deliberateZeros: flow_perp_spot_bear_divergence (0.109/0.144/0.100), mfi_oversold (0.205/0.020/0.071), rel_roc_negative (0.003), trend_adx_trending, ma_sma200_below, structure_fvg_approach. The last is a direct reversal of an earlier design that weighted it at 3: it measured 0.392/0.451 against 0.707/0.935 twenty-four hours earlier, too unstable to weight on a one-day reading.

twoSpecErrorsCaughtBeforeCompile: The three tpoShape clauses were specified with the key `value`. The compile schema's label clause requires {kind, column, op, label} with additionalProperties false, so all three would have been refused. Changed to `label`.

A DEV_POC_ABOVE condition read tpoPOC_close_spread, a header the spec itself described as inferred by symmetry and never emitted. Dropped along with its column, taking the payload from 7 columns / 12 conditions to 6 / 11 and buying byte headroom.

tradeManagement._what: Agent risk envelope set 2026-09-10T19:39Z. Agent revision 1 -> 2. Every bound read from get_trading_config_catalog first; nothing guessed.

whyEachNumber.maxConcurrentExposureUsd 25: Below the wallet, so the agent can never commit more than it holds. Registry max is 250; the default 100 exceeds the wallet and was rejected on that basis.
whyEachNumber.maxCumulativeDrawdownUsd 10: Lifetime realized-loss stop, about 30 percent of the wallet. Must be at or below the ceiling - it is.
whyEachNumber.maxDailyLossUsd 5: Per-UTC-day realized-loss stop, about 15 percent of the wallet. This is the number that actually protects the account.
whyEachNumber.maxDailyTrades 2: Caps churn. Note the measured risk: on the reference fleet, FAILED fills appear to count, so two failures can end a day.
whyEachNumber.maxLeverage 1: No leverage. Registry minimum, and the whole fleet runs at 1.
whyEachNumber.minAllocationUsd 10: The registry FLOOR (minimumAllocationUsd 10). It cannot be set lower.
whyEachNumber.balanceThresholdUsd 15: Minimum equity to allow trading. Set below the 25 ceiling so the drawdown stop binds first: 33.56 minus 10 is 23.56, still above 15.
whyEachNumber.maxSlippageBps 300: Platform default, inside the measured 1-1000 registry band.
whyEachNumber.positionSizePresets 45/60/75: FORCED BY ARITHMETIC, not preference. The schema requires (smallPct/100) x ceiling x floor(maxLeverage) >= max(10, minAllocationUsd). With leverage 1 and the registry floor of 10, that is smallPct x ceiling >= 1000. At a ceiling of 25 the smallest legal smallPct is 40; 45 was chosen for margin. A small account against a 10 USD exchange floor cannot have small percentage presets.

measuredConsequence.feasibilityAdvisory: smallestOrderUsd 25, orderFloorUsd 10 - the config is feasible, smallest order clears the exchange floor.
measuredConsequence.implication: The smallest order this config can place is 25 USD and the exposure ceiling is also 25, so exactly ONE position can be open at a time. That is a tight and deliberate outcome.
measuredConsequence.FUNDING REQUIREMENT: Because the smallest order is 25 USD, allocating LESS than 25 USD to this agent means no order can ever be placed. Allocate at least 25 of the 33.56.

riskRewardIsAStrategyField.note: R:R, the stop-loss ATR multiples and the ATR floor live on the STRATEGY (3d720de3), not the agent. They were set at creation. 1.5 means the target sits 1.5x the stop distance; raising it toward 3 would cut fill rate, which works against the goal of seeing it trigger.
